transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Um, well, I came in because... I know this is going to sound kind of hard to explain, but I've been completely convinced that one of my MBA classmates and this startup advisor I know are quietly coordinating opportunities for me. Like, they'll make certain comments in class, or I'll get these Slack messages, and I can just tell they're coded signals about exactly where my career is supposed to go. 

Which, actually, speaking of Slack, they just updated the whole interface at my company, and as an operations manager, it has been a total nightmare. I had to spend my entire Tuesday just retraining my team on the new channel layouts. I ended up having to buy everyone coffee just to keep morale up. I went to that new cafe on 4th Street—the one with the oat milk draft lattes? It's amazing, but honestly way too expensive for a daily thing. I usually just use my French press at home because the beans I get from this local roaster are just as good... 

Wait, I'm sorry, what was I saying? Oh, right, why I'm here. Yeah, just... the coded messages and the signals from my classmate. It's just been taking up a lot of my headspace lately.
How do these signals from your classmate and the startup advisor make you feel? Do they feel like a source of stress, or do they give you a sense that things are unfolding according to a plan?

I guess... I don't really know if I'd call it stressful. It's more like, yeah, like things are unfolding exactly how they're supposed to. Like a really detailed project plan. 

Which, actually, speaking of plans, I just had to migrate our entire operations team over to Asana from Trello this month, and it has been such a headache. I mean, the color-coding alone took me hours to set up yesterday. I'm really particular about color-coding. I even bought this special set of highlighters for my physical desk planner—they're these pastel Japanese highlighters, Mildliners, I think? They don't bleed through the paper at all. I was at this little stationery shop downtown getting them, and they had this huge display of vintage stamps that I ended up looking at for like forty-five minutes. I used to collect stamps when I was a kid. My grandfather gave me his old album, and it had all these really cool ones from the 1960s... 

Wait, I completely lost my train of thought. I'm sorry, you were asking about the startup advisor?

Can you tell me more about your belief that your classmate and the startup advisor are sending you coded signals? Have you considered that they might just be making normal comments or messages without any hidden meaning?

I mean, I get why you'd ask that. Normal people make normal comments, right? But no, it's... it's too specific. Like, he'll mention "leveraging synergistic growth" in a case study discussion, and then three hours later, the advisor will Slack me an article about scaling operations in emerging markets. It's a clear roadmap. They're quietly coordinating it all for me, I just know it. 

Which is funny, because speaking of emerging markets, my cousin just moved to Singapore for this massive tech role, and she was telling me how hard it was to find an apartment there. She ended up having to hire this relocation specialist who charged her an absolute fortune. I told her she should have just used this app I found for short-term leases, but she's always been kind of stubborn like that. We used to fight over the TV remote when we were little, and she would literally hide the batteries so I couldn't watch cartoons. I really loved those old Saturday morning cartoons, you know? The ones with the commercials for those sugary cereals that turned the milk pink... 

Sorry, I did it again, didn't I? I just... yeah, I don't think they're normal comments. The signals are just too perfectly timed to be a coincidence.
Can you describe how your thoughts usually feel to you—do they flow in a clear, connected way, or do they sometimes feel jumbled, disconnected, or hard to follow?

I guess lately they don't really flow in a clear way. It's more like... my mind has just been jumping around so fast. Like, I'll be thinking about market expansion strategies, and then suddenly I'm thinking about my MBA coursework, and then I'm mentally redesigning my team's org chart, and then I'm wondering if I should move abroad like my cousin. It's all moving so quickly that I'll literally open five different Google Docs on my laptop and completely forget which idea I was even trying to write down first. 

Which is so frustrating because I usually keep my Google Drive incredibly organized. I have this whole folder system with emojis for different projects. Like, a little briefcase for work, a graduation cap for school. I actually spent like three hours last weekend just reorganizing my bookmarks bar on Chrome to match it. I found this really cool extension that color-coordinates your tabs, and it reminded me of this paint-by-numbers kit I used to have. I loved those things. I had this one of a lighthouse on a cliff, and I accidentally spilled the blue paint all over the carpet... my mom was so mad she made me scrub it with club soda for an hour. 

Wait, sorry. I lost it again. You were asking about my thoughts? Yeah, they just... they feel like they're racing all over the place right now.
Have you ever felt that your thoughts are being read or influenced by others?

No, I don't think anyone is reading my thoughts. I mean, they're sending me signals, sure, but they aren't inside my head or anything. I don't feel like my thoughts are being controlled or read. 

Although, it's funny you mention reading, because I just signed up for this new book club that meets at the local library on Thursday nights. We're supposed to be reading this historical fiction novel about the French Revolution, and I'm only on chapter two because the font is just incredibly small. I don't know why publishers do that. I actually had to go buy a new pair of reading glasses at the pharmacy, the ones with the little tortoiseshell frames. The pharmacist there was so helpful, he actually reminded me of my high school chemistry teacher, Mr. Harrison. He used to wear these ridiculous bow ties every single day. We used to keep a tally on the whiteboard of how many different patterns he had. I think the final count was something like forty-two...

Um, what was I saying? Oh, right. No, no one is reading my thoughts or influencing them. It's just the signals.
Have you ever experienced a period where you felt down or hopeless for most of the day, nearly every day, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

No, I haven't really felt down or hopeless like that. I mean, I'm just so busy right now with all these projects and the signals, there's not really time to feel down. I've actually been feeling pretty energized, honestly. 

Speaking of energy, I was looking into getting solar panels for my house because I watched this documentary on renewable energy the other night. It was fascinating. They showed this whole community in Germany that runs entirely on wind and solar power. It made me think about how much electricity we waste, especially with things like leaving the TV on or keeping the porch light on all night. I actually bought these smart bulbs for my living room that you can control with an app on your phone. You can change the colors and everything. I set them to this deep purple color yesterday because I read somewhere that purple is supposed to stimulate creativity, and I really needed to finish this presentation for work. But then the app crashed, and I had to spend like an hour on the phone with customer service, and the guy on the line had this really thick accent...

Wait, sorry. Hopeless? No, no, I haven't felt like that at all. Just really, really busy.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually upbeat, overly energetic, or so restless that others noticed you were acting out of character?

Yeah, definitely. Most days lately I've just felt unusually switched on, you know? Like really optimistic, like I'm right on the edge of something huge. But at the same time, I've been snapping at people. Like my teammates at work, or my boyfriend, over these tiny delays that normally wouldn't even bother me. 

Like yesterday, my boyfriend was taking forever to pick a restaurant for dinner. We were standing in the kitchen and he was just scrolling and scrolling on his phone, looking at Yelp reviews. And I just lost it. I mean, Yelp isn't even that reliable anymore anyway. Half the reviews are probably fake. I read this article about how some restaurants hire companies to write five-star reviews for them, and they use these bots to upvote them so they show up first. It's so deceptive. It makes you wonder what else is completely fake on the internet. Like those influencer photos where they edit the background to look like they're in Paris but they're actually just in their backyard in Ohio. I actually tried using Photoshop once to edit a picture of my dog, Buster, because his eyes were glowing from the flash, but the software was so complicated. There were all these layers and masks and I ended up accidentally turning his fur green. 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right. Upbeat and energetic. Yeah, I've been feeling really on top of things, but just getting annoyed really easily when people can't keep up.
